description: Every stable code a surface may branch on. A code is what crosses a boundary; the sentence a reader sees is rendered from it at the last moment, in their language. This file exists because the codes were bare literals repeated across PowerShell, Go and JavaScript with nothing naming them: a code added on one side and forgotten on another stops being recognized, and the surface that missed it reports the state as unknown rather than as an error anyone chases.
rules: A code is lower-case, underscore-separated, and never contains a word a translator would touch.
Every runtime listed under consumedBy must carry the literal. That is the drift this file is checked for: one side learning a code and another not.
rendersAs names the catalog key a reader-facing surface shows for the code. A code with no key is machine-only and says so.
Adding a value to an enumeration is adding a code. It goes here, or some consumer will silently treat it as unknown.
Every entry has one owner, schema version and lifecycle. Deprecation names a replacement and removal release/date; removal moves the wireCode to retiredCodes, and a retired code is never reused.

codes.means: The runner is parked at a step boundary and will not continue until an operator resumes it. The guest stays up and keeps printing, which is why this is a distinct state rather than an absence of progress.
The host's git credential can read the repository it is configured with.
The repository answered and refused. A credential problem, not a network one, and no retry fixes it.
The host was given no repository to read. Distinct from denied: there is nothing to grant access to.
Nothing has asked yet. An absence of evidence, which a surface must not render as a failure.
The service could not reach the authority needed to validate the supplied lab token. This is an availability condition, not a rejected credential.
The service has no configured authority with which to validate a credential, so state-changing operations remain disabled.
A cycle entry began. Carries index, total, name and kind, so a consumer can build a transcript outline without reading the rendered rule.
A cycle entry finished, with its outcome as a lower-case token rather than the word the transcript prints.

The host can run a host refresh now: a rung above the probe is qualified here, every listener route dependency resolves, and the protocol matches. The Config page shows its refresh control only for this value.
The host cannot run a host refresh; the capability reason says why. Also what an answering server without a refresh field means.
No rung above the probe is qualified on this host type, so nothing a refresh could do would act.
The host-refresh protocol version file is missing, unreadable or not the version this listener speaks.
The private request journal could not be read, so admission cannot be decided safely.
The listener does not know its host type, so it cannot name a rung ladder to advertise.
The capability could not be computed at all; it is reported as unavailable rather than guessed.

A command a worker-backed listener route calls does not resolve in the listener runspace; the route refuses (503) and the capability reads unavailable. Machine-facing reason; the reply sentence comes from its key.
This host holds a valid remote-refresh verifier key, so pool-control can request a refresh with a proof.
No remote-refresh verifier key is installed on this host; only local and loopback refresh are possible.
A remote-refresh verifier key is present but unusable (malformed, wrong host, or not private).
Remote refresh is not qualified on this platform, whatever keys exist.
No host-refresh request holds the host.
A host-refresh request is queued or running on the host.
A host refresh ended with restoration still owed (services, runner, listener or controls); the same request can be resumed and a new one is refused meanwhile.
The listener could not tell whether a host refresh holds the host; the capability is unavailable in that case.
Accepted and waiting for its worker; also the start-cycle reply action for an accepted start.
A worker holds the request and is repairing the host. Also the host-diagnostic worker phase while its run is in progress.
The request reached a verdict and holds no outstanding obligation; also the replay action and the start-cycle and diagnostic terminal phase.
A host refresh refused before changing anything (state and verdict).
A host refresh gave up after repeated attempts; its recovery record is retained.
The refresh changed something and the host converged: probe responsive, services, listener and runner restored.
The refresh found nothing to repair and changed nothing.
The refresh, or a start-cycle or diagnostic worker, failed with nothing left armed; also the diagnostic phase a failed run ends in.
The refresh acted but restoration or readiness is incomplete.
The refresh ended with the hypervisor still not answering its probe.
The refresh worker process started and is loading its module set.
The refresh worker holds the lifetime lock and has claimed the request.
The refresh worker is recording the recovery snapshot before any change.
The refresh worker is probing the hypervisor.
The refresh worker is running repair rungs.
The refresh worker is restoring services, the listener and the runner.
The refresh worker is recording its verdict.
The refresh request reached its final state; the Config page stops polling on it.
The operator should resume the same request on the host.
The operator should start the runner; no recorded launch could be reused.
The operator should grant the automation permission the hypervisor client needs.
The operator should sign in to a desktop session on the host.
The operator should review and dispose of outstanding recovery obligations.
The repair needs administrator rights the worker does not have.
The hypervisor's command-line client is missing on the host.
An answering host omitted the refresh capability, which reads as unavailable (an older listener).
A host advertised a refresh protocol this aggregator does not speak.
A host advertised a refresh capability outside the allowed vocabulary.
A host's control-status reply could not be read (too large, not JSON).
The aggregator could not reach the host to read its capability.
The last observation of a host's refresh capability is too old to trust.
The aggregator has never read this host's refresh capability.
Another host operation (a host refresh or a start-cycle) holds the host; the reply names which in activeKind. Also the start-cycle worker reason when a refresh became active.
A known host-refresh request id arrived with a different tier or ceiling.
A host-refresh request id that was refused, expired or abandoned; it is never run again.
The listener could not launch the detached worker; a host-refresh request stays queued and can be retried, a start-cycle reservation is removed.
Four request bodies are already being read; the caller retries after Retry-After.
The refresh journal or reservation store could not record the request.
The host advertises no refresh it can run; nothing was admitted.
The private state root or a worker directory under it could not be secured; the route fails closed.
A host-refresh body exceeded 4096 bytes, declared or counted.
A host-refresh body did not complete within two seconds of the request.
A host-refresh body was not a strict JSON object.
A host-refresh body named a key outside requestId, tier and maxRung.
A host-refresh body named a local-only safety switch (force, hard stop, service selection, config path).
A host-refresh body carried a value outside its field domain.
A host-refresh request did not declare application/json.
A worker-backed route or worker failed unexpectedly; the listener answered 500 instead of tearing the connection.
The listener could not load the refresh-proof verifier for a non-loopback caller; it refuses.
A host answered a pool-control refresh with a reply outside the documented table.
The detached worker was launched (host-refresh admission, or the runner a start-cycle started).
The same request is already claimed by a live or unknown worker; nothing new was launched.
The host diagnostic is still running; ask again after Retry-After.
The operation holding the host is a host refresh.
The operation holding the host is a start-cycle.
A non-loopback refresh carried no refresh proof.
The refresh proof is not the eight-field wire shape.
The refresh proof names a version this verifier does not accept.
The refresh proof MAC does not verify.
The refresh proof is for another host.
The refresh proof is for another request id.
The refresh proof binds another tier or ceiling.
The refresh proof lifetime is longer than allowed or inverted.
The refresh proof is issued in the future beyond the skew allowance.
The refresh proof expired.
Remote refresh is not qualified on this platform.
The requested tier or ceiling is not allowed remotely (restart tier, Order 0-4 only).
No remote-refresh verifier key is installed on the host.
The host's remote-refresh verifier key is unusable.
The verifier itself failed (including a listener that does not know its host id); refused.
pool-control holds no refresh authority or credential, so it cannot request a refresh.
The pool-control refresh route needs the separately provisioned refresh credential.
Too many failed refresh-credential attempts; retry later.
The start-cycle worker cleared the controls, cleaned up and started or woke the runner.
The start-cycle worker made its decision but the cleanup failed or the runner state was unknown.
The start-cycle worker woke a live runner through the restart request instead of starting another.
The start-cycle worker left the runner alone (its state was unknown, or its launch failed).
Another operation held the lifetime repair lock; the start-cycle worker changed nothing.
The start-cycle worker's reservation was no longer its own; it changed nothing.
The runner's state could not be positively established after cleanup; no runner was started.
The bounded VM cleanup exited non-zero or did not complete; the runner decision still followed.
The bounded VM cleanup reached its time limit; the runner decision still followed.
The start-cycle worker could not launch the runner.
